I have been farming this land in Quzhou for forty years. My 12 mu is all I have, and I know every piece of it. It is October now, so the first thing on my mind is getting the winter wheat sown before the soil gets too cold. I will plant all 12 mu to wheat — leaving land fallow makes no sense when the household still needs grain and cash.

For the wheat, I will buy improved seed from the township supply shop, maybe something like Jimai 22 or whatever variety the neighbors had success with last year. Before sowing, I will run the rotary tiller over the whole field to break up the maize stubble and level the ground. I know the soil here is tired, so I will spread about 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer as a base, and then topdress with urea twice — once when the wheat turns green in spring, and again at jointing. My well gives me enough water for four irrigations: right after sowing to help the seeds settle, one before winter so the young plants do not freeze-dry, one at jointing when the wheat starts growing fast, and one at grain filling. I will spray herbicide once after emergence, and if I see aphids or rust, I will spray insecticide or fungicide once more. After forty years, I expect about 500 kg per mu from this wheat if the weather is normal.

Come early June, as soon as the wheat is cut, I have only a few days to get the summer maize in. Time is short, so I will not waste it tilling. I will sow the maize directly into the wheat stubble — no-tillage — using hybrid seed. Everyone around here uses hybrids like Denghai 605; the yield is much better than anything else. I will put down compound fertilizer at planting, and then spread urea when the maize is about knee-high and hungry for nitrogen. Maize needs less water than wheat on this plain, so I will irrigate twice with my well: once around the big growth stage if the rains fail, and once at tasseling-silking because that is when the ears are set — without water then, the yield drops badly. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide once for the corn borer. I reckon I can get about 550 kg per mu from the maize.

My family has off-farm income, so I can afford these inputs, but I am not wasteful. After four decades, I know that adding more fertilizer or water beyond what I just described does not pay back in extra grain.
